headline: Scientists map genes of four endangered Asian hornbills
meta_description: Indian researchers create first-ever reference genomes for four threatened hornbill species, opening new paths for conservation.
summary_short: Scientists have decoded the genetic blueprints of four endangered Asian hornbills, revealing their evolutionary past and potential resilience.
body:
Scientists from India have decoded the genetic blueprints of four threatened Asian hornbill species—a breakthrough that may reshape how conservationists protect these vulnerable birds. Researchers at the Nature Conservation Foundation in Mysore and the CSIR–Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology in Hyderabad assembled high-quality reference genomes for the great hornbill, rufous-necked hornbill, Malabar pied hornbill, and wreathed hornbill. Before this study, complete genome information existed for only two of the 32 Asian hornbill species worldwide. By combining two types of DNA sequencing—short- and long-read methods—the team created detailed genetic maps that minimize errors and reveal the species' deep histories.

The genomes tell stories stretching back millions of years. Using statistical modeling, researchers traced how climate swings during the Pleistocene epoch, between 2.5 million and 11,000 years ago, shrank the populations of all four species. The widely distributed wreathed hornbill fared better than its cousins, maintaining a larger population through those unstable periods. These findings matter because genetic diversity directly determines whether a population can adapt to future threats. "Genetic variation or diversity is crucial to the adaptive potential and long-term resilience of populations," explained Meghana Natesh, a conservation geneticist at WWF India.

The real power of this research lies in what it enables next. By comparing the genomes of different hornbill species, scientists can now link specific traits—from behavior to physical characteristics—to the genetic variations that produce them. This foundation lets conservationists evaluate which populations are strongest, where to focus protection efforts, and how to manage breeding programs for maximum genetic health. It transforms hornbill conservation from educated guesswork into precision science.
quick_facts: Four threatened Asian hornbill species now have complete reference genomes
Only two of 32 Asian hornbill species had full genome data before this study
Climate shifts 2.5 million years ago reduced population sizes of all four species
Researchers used short- and long-read DNA sequencing to minimize genetic mapping errors
